lower_retrospective.note: lower CUSUM designed on the weeks <= 34 rate and run from run 1; illustrates when the improvement would have been confirmed; the reference rate is estimated from the same data

shift_simulation.convention: zero-state step shift at run 1; weekly subgroups cycle through the observed weekly sizes from a random start week; detection probability is P(first signal in the direction of the shift within h runs); at ratio 1 any signal counts, as a false alarm

laney_p_prime_phase1_sigma.label: weekly Laney p′, Phase I-centred σ_z

cusum_upper_matched.label: Bernoulli CUSUM, upper, matched to p-chart

cusum_lower_matched.label: Bernoulli CUSUM, lower, matched to g-chart

segmentation.rule: split a segment while its block-permutation p < 0.05; segments shorter than 60 runs are not tested

p0_reestimate.design_logic: p1 = 2 * p0; h calibrated by simulation to ARL0 = 500 runs at p0 (3000 paths x 8000 runs, seed 20080719); alarms counted with reset on signal, each window charted from a fresh start

rates.post_change_source: changepoint segment after the estimated change

arl_simulation.note: independent Bernoulli streams; censored run lengths count as max_run

overdispersion.model: beta-binomial random effect: every calendar day (or ISO week) of the observed campaign layout draws its own fail probability from a Beta with mean p and intraclass correlation rho; runs within it are Bernoulli at that probability
overdispersion.calibration: rho solved (Brent) so the mean Laney sigma_z of simulated in-control campaigns at p0, charted on the observed weekly subgroups and centred on their own rate, equals the observed all-weeks sigma_z; verified on fresh streams

detection_settings.note: same seed, stream count and start weeks as shift_simulation, so the independent rows reproduce its table and every condition shares common random numbers
